correctness.rationale: Conditionally on the full joint past, a fresh uniform proposal is rejected with probability sum_i(d_i/D)/n=1/n. Repeating without updating degrees until acceptance gives exactly Q_i, and the first proposals themselves are independent choices for the uniform comparison. Deterministic conditional rejection probabilities imply independence by iterated conditioning. The log moment generating function is m(e^t-1) log N+O_m,t(1); choosing small signed t gives summable tail bounds on dyadic N, and monotonicity interpolates because consecutive dyadic logarithms have ratio tending to one. Changing H targets alters at most two final vertex degrees per edit, so histogram TV is at most 2H/N. For uniform attachment a nonseed birth rank i has independent Bernoulli increments, m per old count n from i to N-1. On ranks i/N bounded away from zero the Poisson approximation is uniform (the summed squared probabilities are O(1/N)), and its mean is uniformly m log(N/i)+o(1). A Riemann sum and removal of the lower-rank cutoff yield the exponential–Poisson mixture m^r/(m+1)^{r+1}. Each coordinate is 2/N-Lipschitz in each of m(N-2) independent choices; concentration, Borel–Cantelli and truncation of a probability limit give almost-sure TV convergence, then transfer by the coupling. The fixed seed contributes only 2/N and m=1 also obeys every estimate.
residual_risks: The frozen finite run was not replayed and does not prove an almost-sure limit. The rate is an upper bound on empirical histogram discrepancy, not graph-level total variation or a lower bound.
